STEP 1 - Scene: Two halves of cooked corn on the cob (yellow sweet corn, cut crosswise, showing the pale cut center) on a white plate. Diced orange vegetable (likely carrot or squash) sits on a separate plate at the bottom-right edge, which is not part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White oval/triangular plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Corn cob pieces (two cross-cut sections, one stacked on the other)
- Nothing else visible on this plate (no oil or sauce visible)

STEP 4 - Area: The two corn pieces together cover about 14% of the plate (each roughly 7 cm diameter, ~38 cm^2 each, plus the stacked overlap; ~75 cm^2 total ≈ 14%).

STEP 5 - Volume: Corn pieces are dense cylinders about 3.5 to 4 cm tall when stacked. 75 cm^2 x 3.5 cm ≈ 260 ml gross envelope.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn kernels on cob are fairly dense as a solid cylinder; use density ~0.7 g/ml for cut cob sections (kernels plus cob with air gaps). 260 ml x 0.7 ≈ 180 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sweet corn ≈ 96 kcal/100 g (boiled, kernels with cob portion, roughly similar). 180 g x 0.96 ≈ 173 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two cut corn-cob sections of this size (about 180 g total) is plausible. Roughly 170 kcal is reasonable for this amount of boiled sweet corn.

Estimated total: about 180 g, about 170 kcal.
